newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES WEAKER ON HARD UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES WEAKER ON HARD UNITS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar closed weaker against hard currencies on Thursday under import pressure, with dealers saying an element of speculation also seemed to have crept into the market.
"It looks like import pressure is still on but there could also be speculation," one dealer said.
He said some market players could possibly be pushing the rates up for the benefit of tobacco producers ahead of the annual sales set to commence in April.
"But anyway when the tobacco inflows start coming in the dollar should start appreciating," the dealer added.
The local unit finished Thursday trade at 11.2800/2900 against the U.S. dollar, down from 11.2575/2675 at Wednesday's close and was quoted at 18.0200/0400 from 17.9690/9960 against sterling.
It slipped to 6.7300/7500 from 6.6700/6900 against the mark but was quoted a touch firmer on the rand at 2.5400/5600 compared to 2.5415/5455.
